_DEVICE_NOTE_: Apple M4 laptop GPU (MPS) in Low Power Mode, half-width ResNet-9 (1.68 M parameters), 20 epochs per model; on a Kaggle/Colab GPU the notebook automatically uses full width and 30 epochs
_CURVES_TEXT_:
| Model | Params | Val acc | Test top-1 | Test top-5 | Test loss |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lecture deep CNN | 0.84 M | 57.5% | 57.6% | 85.8% | 1.50 |
| ResNet-9 + SE | 1.68 M | 69.6% | **69.6%** | **91.5%** | 1.16 |

ResNet-9 is **+12 pp** better in top-1. With 100 classes the lecture CNN is clearly *under*fitting rather than overfitting: train accuracy (50%, measured with dropout and augmentation) stays below validation, and its curve flattens after ~12 epochs — 0.8 M parameters and heavy dropout (up to 0.5) are too little capacity for 100 classes. ResNet-9 keeps rising until the end (the OneCycle lr decay in the last third adds ~12 pp), and its train accuracy (82%) is now above validation: it uses its capacity. Both would gain from more epochs. Top-5 accuracy is far higher (91.5%): the correct class is almost always among the candidates, the hard part is choosing between similar fine classes.
_ERRORS_TEXT_: Hardest classes: otter (33%), girl (37%), lizard (42%), seal and mouse (44%); easiest: orange, road (94%), motorcycle (93%), sunflower (92%). The top confusions are *semantically* close pairs: maple ↔ oak ↔ pine tree, girl ↔ woman ↔ boy, otter → seal, dolphin → whale, bowl → plate, bus → streetcar. **35% of all errors stay inside the true superclass** (if errors were random, ~4% would), and the superclass of the prediction is right in 80% of cases. So the network learns the coarse hierarchy well; what is missing at 32×32 is the fine detail that separates a girl from a woman or a maple from an oak.
_CONCLUSION_TEXT_:
1. CIFAR-100 has the same images as CIFAR-10 in format, but 100 classes with only 500 training images each, so it is much harder: chance is 1%.
2. The lecture deep CNN reaches **57.6%** top-1 / 85.8% top-5 and underfits; the CIFAR-10 recipe (ResNet-9 + SE, augmentation, OneCycle, label smoothing) reaches **69.6%** top-1 / **91.5%** top-5 with the same 20 epochs.
3. Errors are mostly between semantically close classes (trees, people, aquatic mammals): 35% of mistakes stay in the true superclass.
4. On a cloud GPU (Kaggle/Colab) the same notebook runs the full-width ResNet-9 for 30 epochs, which usually adds several more points (published ResNet-9-type results are ~75%).
